statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the minimum positive integer not expressible from nums. Here an integer x is expressible from nums if there exist k ≥ 1 and indices 0 ≤ i1 < i2 < ... < ik < len(nums) such that (nums[i1] | nums[i2] | ... | nums[ik]) = x, where | denotes bitwise OR. Thus r ≥ 1; r is not expressible from nums; and every integer y with 1 ≤ y < r is expressible from nums. Equivalently, r is the least power of two 2^k (k ≥ 0) that does not occur as a value nums[i] for any i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums).
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and 1 ≤ r ≤ 1073741824, where 1073741824 = 2^30.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exists an integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ 30 such that r = 2^k.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every integer y with 1 ≤ y < r, there exist k ≥ 1 and indices 0 ≤ i1 < i2 < ... < ik < len(nums) such that (nums[i1] | nums[i2] | ... | nums[ik]) = y.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and there do not exist k ≥ 1 and indices 0 ≤ i1 < i2 < ... < ik < len(nums) such that (nums[i1] | nums[i2] | ... | nums[ik]) = r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ 30 and 2^k < r, there exists an integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 2^k.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1 if and only if there is no integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 1.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; if there exists an integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 1, and there is no integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 2, then r = 2.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and, for every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ 30, if there is no integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 2^k, then r ≤ 2^k.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and, for every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ 30, if for every integer j with 0 ≤ j < k there exists an integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 2^j, then r ≥ 2^k.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1073741824 if and only if for every integer k with 0 ≤ k < 30 there exists an integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 2^k.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.

statement: Let r be the result on nums and r' be the result on nums'. The function does not fail on nums or on nums'. If for every integer v, (there exists an integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v) if and only if (there exists an integer j with 0 <= j < len(nums') and nums'[j] = v), then r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= len(nums') <= 100000, for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and for every integer j with 0 <= j < len(nums'), 1 <= nums'[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let r be the result on nums and r' be the result on nums'. The function does not fail on nums or on nums'. If for every integer v, (there exists an integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v) implies (there exists an integer j with 0 <= j < len(nums') and nums'[j] = v), then r <= r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000, 1 <= len(nums') <= 100000, for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and for every integer j with 0 <= j < len(nums'), 1 <= nums'[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (that is, it does not fail) for every input nums satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000 and for every integer i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000000000.
